instructions: Finely chop the onion and the garlic. Cut the red pepper, green pepper, carrots and zucchini into 1/2-inch pieces.
Put a large, wide pot over medium heat and add the 1/4 cup olive oil. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook for 3 minutes, until it starts to soften.
Add the peppers, carrots and zucchini. Cover and cook for 6 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the carrots start to soften.
Add the garlic and the paprika and stir for 30 seconds. Keep it moving so the paprika doesn't burn.
Stir in the tomato sauce, the black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Drain and rinse the beans. Add them to the pot with 2 1/2 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 6 minutes. If you like it thicker, mash a few spoonfuls of the beans against the side of the pot.
Stir in the last 1/2 tsp salt. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve in bowls.
method_notes: Bonviveur (4.9 from 35 votes) builds a sofrito of onion, peppers, carrot and zucchini, adds paprika and tomato, then the beans and water; its canned-bean version is the lead, doubled for 4. Karlos Arguinano's 25-minute version cooks the vegetables covered and adds canned beans with a little tomato sauce, which is why the vegetables are covered here. Bonviveur blends part of the sofrito back in for body; that step is left out to keep it quick and to avoid a blender, and mashing a few beans does the same job. Vegan and gluten-free as written. Honest total is about 32 minutes.
